ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

性质的决策原因和经验教训)\\n\\n## 经验教训\\n\\n- [2026-05-14] **MCKP 在低压缩率(2x)下反而不如 uniform**：budget=0.5 时 uniform 8-bit PPL=10.10 vs MCKP PPL=10.66。原因：PPL profiler 在 4-bit 和 8-bit 之间分辨率坍缩（delta≈0），solver 误判降级免费。uniform 8-bit 已近无损（+0.29 vs FP16）。论文 Claim 2 限定为 \\\"moderate-to-aggressive compression (≥4x)\\\"。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Greedy total_distortion=0 解释**：大多数中间/后层 head 在单独量化到 2-bit 时 profiled delta ≈ 0，但联合 68 heads 量化到 2-bit 导致 compounding error (PPL 32.45)。Additive profiling model 的根本盲点。cardinality constraint 作为 compounding non-additivity 的正则化。\\n- [2026-05-14] **8x 压缩下两者都不实用**：MCKP PPL=906.78 vs uniform PPL=14758.92。虽然 MCKP 好 16x，但绝对 PPL 太高。论文中 8x 作为 stress test — \\\"even at extreme compression, L0 protection prevents total collapse\\\"。\\n- [2026-05-14] **max_2bit 缩放问题**：Llama/Mistral 256 heads 用 max_2bit=8 仅占 3.1% (vs Qwen 112 heads 的 7.1%)。当前先用 8 跑 baseline，后续规划 max_2bit 缩放 ablation（按比例 ~18 for 256 heads）。\\n- [2026-05-14] **HF_HOME 必须显式设置**：服务器上 HF datasets 默认下载会超时。所有 pipeline 脚本必须在 import 前设 `os.environ[\\\"HF_HOME\\\"] = \\\"/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache\\\"` 和 `HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1`。WikiText-2 缓存在 `/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache/datasets/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw-v1/`。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Lowres profiling 对多 head 模型不足**：Llama lowres (16×512) MCKP PPL=8.70 劣于 Uniform=8.47。256 heads + 低分辨率 calibration → delta 高度同质化 → solver 盲目分配。与 Qwen exp_e 完全一致（lowres 恶化 2.52, hires 降到 0.75）。**规则：head 数 >200 的模型必须用 hires profiling (≥64×2048)**。\\n- [2026-05-14] **fp16 eval 在大模型上产生无效结果**：Llama eval 用 fp16 得到 PPL=1.31（overflow），Qwen L27 层 K cache range [-420,234] 也 overflow。**规则：所有 eval 必须用 bf16，禁止 fp16**。已全局扫描修复。\\n- [2026-05-14] **GQA ratio 调节 MCKP 优势幅度**：Qwen GQA 7:1 (112 heads) → MCKP 优势 1.776 PPL (大)。Llama GQA 4:1 (256 heads) → MCKP 优势仅 0.019 PPL (极薄)。原因：高 GQA ratio → 更少 KV heads → head 间异质性更高 → MCKP 优化空间更大。低 GQA ratio → 更多 heads → 更同质 → uniform 已接近最优。论文 framing 需体现这一规律。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Llama L0 sensitivity 远低于 Qwen**：确认。Llama hires 最终 MCKP=8.4498 仅比 uniform=8.4690 好 0.019，说明 Llama heads 间异质性低，L0 不是瓶颈。Claim 1 (heterogeneity) 是 architecture-dependent 特性，非 universal。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Mistral 确认 GQA 4:1 模式——即使 hires 也不够**：Mistral hires MCKP=7.3231 仍劣于 uniform=7.1314。三模型验证完毕：GQA 4:1 (256 heads) 在 4x 压缩下 MCKP 无优势。但 Llama aggressive (5.3x) MCKP=57.6 vs Uniform=2643.8，说明低 GQA 模型在更高压缩率下仍然受益巨大。**规则：论文中 Llama/Mistral 定位为 sensitivity analysis，不作为 universal validation。**\\n- [2026-05-14] **5.3x 是低 GQA 模型的 MCKP sweet spot**：budget=0.1875 (5.3x) 时 selective allocation (128@4bit + 128@2bit) vs all-2bit 产生 45x PPL 差异。8x 时 248/256 heads 被迫 2-bit，优化空间受限 (仅 11% 优势)。原因：5.3x 是 uniform baseline \\\"刚开始严重退化\\\"的拐点，MCKP 的 selective protection 价值最大化。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Cron 监控假阳性**：不使用 W&B 的短实验（solver+eval without training loop）正常退出后被 cron 判为 \\\"process dead 5× with no sentinel/W&B\\\"。这类实验应在脚本结尾写一个 sentinel file (如 `touch /tmp/{exp_id}.done`)，或直接不挂 cron 监控。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Eval pipeline 不一致导致数字混乱**：exp_e 使用了不同于主 pipeline 的 eval 参数（可能是 sequence length 或 stride 不同），导致 baseline=8.82 和 MCKP=9.57。统一 pipeline 给出 baseline=9.81, MCKP hires=10.91, uniform=15.45。**规则：论文使用统一 pipeline 数字，不引用 exp_e 的绝对 PPL。** hires_mckp_reeval (10.9131) 取代 exp_e (9.569)。\\n- [2026-05-14] **bf16 vs fp16 差异可忽略**：qwen_bf16_reeval 确认 baseline delta=0.0006, uniform delta=0.005。在当前 eval pipeline 下 bf16≈fp16，compounding_sweep 等早期 fp16 实验无需 rerun。但 exp_e 的不同 eval pipeline 下差异较大 (baseline 8.82 vs 9.81)——这不是 dtype 问题，是 eval 设置差异。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Solver equivalence confirmed (plan_016)**：greedy+constraint (PPL=11.2312) = MCKP+constraint (PPL=11.23), delta=0.0012（实际=0.0000，0.0012 是 hardcoded 四舍五入导致）。三模型逐头验证：Qwen 112/112 完全匹配，Llama 256/256 完全匹配，Mistral 255/256（唯一差异 head distortion=0 → 无影响）。贡献 100% 来自 cardinality constraint。论文 Claim 2 核心证据。\\n- [2026-05-14] **k ablation 三模型 pattern 完美分化**：(1) Qwen U 形曲线 k=8 最优 (2) Llama 平坦——natural 2-bit count=2，任何 k≥2 给出相同 allocation (3) Mistral 单调递增——k 越小越好但始终劣于 uniform。这个三分格局直接支撑 Claim 3 (heterogeneity-dependent diagnostic)。论文可展示 k vs PPL 三线图作为核心 figure。\\n- [2026-05-14] **Downstream accuracy 验证 PPL 趋势**：MCKP hires avg 0.6857 vs uniform 0.6597 (+2.60pp)，recovery rate 72.8%。ARC-C 上 MCKP 甚至超 baseline (0.5137 vs 0.4957)。PPL 改善确实转化为 downstream 增益，非 PPL-only 的 artifact。\\n- [2026-05-14] **K/V 分离不如 joint 优化**：K/V separated MCKP (11.22) 比 joint K=V MCKP (10.91) 差 +0.303 PPL。根因：V 量化 distortion 几乎为零（per-token quant 天然鲁棒），112 个 V head 全部被分配 4-bit，分离后增加的自由度只让 solver 更激进地压缩 K（16 个 K@2-bit vs joint 的 8 个）。与 KIVI (ICML 2024) 发现一致。论文定位：ablation 确认 joint K=V 分配的充分性。\\n\", \"total_chars\": 4442, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission)
- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026 (11 days from today 2026-05-14)
- Track: Efficient Methods for NLP

## Core Insight

Per-head KV cache quantization sensitivity varies dramatically across architectures, and the effectiveness of non-uniform mixed-precision allocation is fundamentally determined by the degree of this heterogeneity. We provide both the analysis framework — characterizing when non-uniform quantization helps via per-head sensitivity concentration metrics — and a surprisingly simple method fix: a cardinality constraint (≤k heads at 2-bit) that prevents compounding effects from profiler non-additivity and reduces the search space sufficiently that solver choice becomes irrelevant (greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations).

## Core Claims (3 条)

1. **Head sensitivity heterogeneity is architecture-dependent**: Per-KV-head quantization sensitivity is extremely non-uniform within models (Layer 0 heads exhibit ~26× higher 2-bit delta than average in Qwen), but the *degree* of heterogeneity varies across architectures. High-GQA-ratio models (Qwen, 7:1, 112 heads) show high concentration (Top-5% heads account for 59-66% of total distortion), while low-GQA-ratio models (Llama/Mistral, 4:1, 256 heads) show lower concentration (34-59%). This heterogeneity degree determines the optimization headroom for non-uniform allocation.

2. **Cardinality constraint is the primary intervention; profiling benefit is architecture-dependent**: On non-consecutive discrete bit-widths {2,4,8,16}, unconstrained allocation — whether by greedy (PPL 32.45) or MCKP (PPL 36.92) — produces catastrophic results because per-head independent profiling distortions compound non-additively when many heads are simultaneously assigned extreme quantization. A cardinality constraint (max_2bit≤k) is a simple and sufficient condition: it prevents compounding AND reduces the feasible set to a regime where solver choice is irrelevant — constrained greedy and constrained MCKP produce identical bit allocations and PPL (Δ=0.0000, both 11.2312). The profiling benefit beyond the constraint (hires vs lowres) is architecture-dependent: substantial on high-heterogeneity models (Qwen), marginal on low-heterogeneity ones. The optimal k is determinable via small-scale compounding effect test (plan_004).

Each model uses its optimal k determined by k ablation (Qwen k=8, Llama k=2, Mistral k=4). The causal predictor is per-head sensitivity concentration (Top-5% > 0.50 → non-uniform recommended; directional evidence, n=3). Under aggressive compression (≥5×), constrained allocation prevents catastrophic collapse even on low-heterogeneity models (Llama 5.3×: constrained PPL 57.60 vs uniform 2-bit 2644). This provides practitioners a diagnostic for when to invest in mixed-precision KV cache quantization.

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: KV cache quantization typically applies uniform bit-width across all heads. Per-head mixed-precision allocation promises better quality-compression tradeoffs, but two fundamental questions remain unanswered: (1) *when* does non-uniform allocation actually help — i.e., under what architectural and compression conditions does the added complexity pay off? (2) *how* to make existing allocation algorithms (greedy, MCKP) work correctly on hardware-aligned discrete bit-widths {2,4,8,16} where they currently fail catastrophically?

- **Existing approaches & gaps**: RateQuant (May 2026) provides R-D optimal per-head allocation via continuous closed-form (Theorem 2) and discrete greedy (Algorithm 1, optimal on consecutive integers {2,...,6} per Proposition 6). However, on hardware-aligned non-consecutive sets {2,4,8,16}, RateQuant's greedy produces PPL 32.45 (vs optimal ~11.23) — the polymatroid structure that guarantees greedy optimality breaks. Moreover, unconstrained MCKP fares even worse (PPL 36.92) due to compounding effects from profiler non-additivity. Critically, neither RateQuant nor ARKV addresses *when* non-uniform allocation is beneficial.

- **Our framing**: We present a systematic study of per-head KV cache quantization sensitivity across architectures and identify a surprisingly simple fix for the failure of existing algorithms on hardware-aligned bit-widths: a cardinality constraint limiting the number of heads assigned to extreme quantization levels. This single intervention (a) prevents compounding effects, (b) reduces the search space to where solver choice is irrelevant — greedy and MCKP produce identical optimal allocations, and (c) can be parameterized via a small-scale compounding test. Beyond the method, we establish that the benefit of non-uniform allocation is architecture-dependent and quantifiable via per-head sensitivity concentration, providing practitioners a diagnostic for when mixed-precision is worthwhile.

- **Our framing**: We present a systematic study of per-head KV cache quantization sensitivity across architectures and identify a surprisingly simple fix for the failure of existing algorithms on hardware-aligned bit-widths: a cardinality constraint limiting the number of heads assigned to extreme quantization levels. This single intervention (a) prevents compounding effects, (b) reduces the search space to where solver choice is irrelevant — greedy and MCKP produce identical optimal allocations, and (c) can be parameterized via a small-scale compounding test. Beyond the method, we establish that the benefit of non-uniform allocation is architecture-dependent and quantifiable via per-head sensitivity concentration, providing practitioners a diagnostic for when mixed-precision is worthwhile.

- **Headline result template**: "We show that a simple cardinality constraint (≤k heads at 2-bit) is a simple and sufficient condition for correct per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths {2,4,8,16}: without it, both greedy and MCKP fail catastrophically (PPL 32-37); with it, both produce identical near-optimal allocations (PPL 11.23). This constrained allocation achieves 27.3% PPL improvement on architectures with high head sensitivity heterogeneity (Qwen, GQA 7:1), while our analysis shows uniform quantization suffices for low-heterogeneity architectures — providing the first systematic framework for deciding when non-uniform KV cache quantization is worthwhile."

## "When Does Non-Uniform Allocation Help?" — Analysis Chapter

Three case studies representing the spectrum of heterogeneity:

| Case | Model | Top-5% Conc. | Constrained vs Uniform (4×) | Role in Paper |
|------|-------|--------------|------------------------------|---------------|
| **Positive** | Qwen2.5-7B (GQA 7:1) | 0.59-0.66 | **+27.3% (11.23 vs 15.45)** | Primary showcase |
| **Marginal** | Llama-3.1-8B (GQA 4:1) | 0.34-0.59 | +0.2% (8.45 vs 8.47) | Boundary condition |
| **Negative** | Mistral-7B-v0.3 (GQA 4:1, SWA) | 0.42 | -0.4% (7.16 vs 7.13) | Genuine negative: profiler zero-signal (total_distortion≈0.0) |

**Compression amplifies benefit**: Even on low-heterogeneity Llama, aggressive 5.3× compression yields constrained PPL=57.60 vs uniform 2-bit=2643.77 (45× better).

**Practical diagnostic** (directional evidence, n=3): Top-5% concentration > 0.50 → non-uniform allocation recommended. Below 0.50 → uniform suffices at moderate compression; non-uniform still valuable at aggressive compression.

## Solver Equivalence Evidence (plan_016, CONFIRMED ✅)

| Method | PPL | Bit Distribution | Budget |
|--------|-----|-------------------|--------|
| Greedy unconstrained | 32.45 | {2:68, 4:30, 8:4, 16:10} | 0.25 |
| MCKP unconstrained | 36.92 | — | 0.25 |
| **Greedy + max_2bit=8** | **11.2312** | **{8:4, 4:100, 2:8}** | **0.25** |
| **MCKP + max_2bit=8** | **11.2312** | **{8:4, 4:100, 2:8}** | **0.25** |
| Uniform 4-bit | 15.4454 | all 4-bit | 0.25 |

Key takeaway: The constraint is the primary intervention — without it, both solvers fail; with it, solver choice is irrelevant (Δ=0.0000). This powerfully demonstrates the constraint is THE contribution.

**Aggressive compression** (Llama): At 5.3× compression, constrained PPL=57.60 vs uniform 2-bit=2643.77 — prevents catastrophic collapse even on low-heterogeneity architectures.

## Differentiation from RateQuant

| Aspect | RateQuant | Ours |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Bit-width selection | Greedy on consecutive integers {2,...,6} (Prop. 6 optimal) + continuous closed-form (Thm. 2) | Cardinality-constrained allocation on hardware-aligned {2,4,8,16}-bit |
| Distortion model | Additive, parametric D(b)=α·β^{-b} | Additive + cardinality regularization for non-additivity |
| Compounding effects | Acknowledged (Appendix M) but unaddressed | **Core contribution**: cardinality constraint prevents compounding; first quantitative evidence |
| Action space | Consecutive integers (polymatroid → greedy optimal) | Non-consecutive hardware-aligned (polymatroid breaks → constraint needed, solver doesn't matter) |
| Solver requirement | Greedy (provably optimal in their setting) | **Any solver** — constrained greedy = constrained MCKP (Δ=0.0000 PPL) |
| K/V allocation | Asymmetric K/V budget (e.g. K=2.85, V=2.15) | MCKP/greedy treats K/V heads as independent items (natural extension) |
| **Applicability analysis** | **Not addressed — assumes non-uniform always helps** | **Systematic study of when non-uniform allocation is beneficial (new contribution)** |

## Venue Fit Risks

- **"The constraint is just a heuristic, not a real contribution"**: Strongest reviewer attack under new framing. Defense: (a) principled motivation from compounding effect non-additivity with first quantitative evidence, (b) constraint parameterization via systematic compounding test, (c) the finding that constraint alone makes solver choice irrelevant is a surprising and practically useful result — practitioners need only add one parameter to existing pipelines.
- **Incrementality over RateQuant**: Defense: (a) RateQuant's greedy is suboptimal unconstrained on {2,4,8,16} (PPL 32.45), (b) our constraint fixes RateQuant's greedy to match MCKP — we're improving their method, not replacing it, (c) applicability analysis is entirely new.
- **Method only strong on one architecture**: Qwen is the only clear success. Mitigate by framing as *analysis contribution*: the finding that non-uniform allocation effectiveness is architecture-dependent is itself valuable. Llama/Mistral are honest negative/marginal results that strengthen credibility.
- **Statistical power of heterogeneity correlation**: n=3 models is too few for significant correlation. Do NOT claim "significant correlation" — use "we observe a consistent trend" or "directional evidence."
- **No eviction arm**: Mention as negative finding; framework extends naturally to eviction.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

1. **"The cardinality constraint is trivial — just cap the extreme allocations"** → (a) Trivial in retrospect, but without it both greedy (PPL 32.45) and MCKP (PPL 36.92) fail catastrophically — the failure mode is non-obvious, (b) principled motivation from compounding effect characterization (plan_004), (c) optimal k selection via systematic small-scale test, (d) the finding that this single intervention eliminates solver complexity is surprising and practically valuable.
2. **"This is just RateQuant with a constraint added"** → (a) We agree — and that's the point: RateQuant's greedy + our constraint achieves identical results to MCKP + constraint, (b) the constraint addresses a real gap: compounding effects on {2,4,8,16} that RateQuant acknowledges but doesn't solve, (c) applicability analysis is new.
3. **"The method only works on Qwen — isn't this a Qwen paper?"** → The analysis contribution generalizes beyond any single model. We characterize the *boundary conditions* of non-uniform quantization, which is more useful than a universally positive but misleading claim.
4. **"How does this work at different compression ratios?"** → Budget sweep across 2×, 4×, 8× (plan_005). Aggressive compression on Llama shows benefit amplifies even on low-heterogeneity models.
5. **"n=3 models is not enough for the heterogeneity claim"** → Acknowledged as limitation. We present directional evidence and a testable hypothesis with the Top-5% concentration diagnostic.
6. **"RateQuant does K/V asymmetric allocation, do you?"** → Framework naturally treats K and V heads as independent items; plan_014 tests K/V separation.
7. **"Where are the downstream task results?"** → ✅ DONE (plan_012): ARC-C +3.16pp, HellaSwag +4.00pp, PIQA +1.25pp, WinoGrande +1.97pp. Avg recovery 72.8% of bf16-to-uniform degradation.
8. **"The profiler distortion=0.0 on Mistral suggests the profiling method is broken"** → Profiler correctly reports near-zero sensitivity differences. Some architectures genuinely have homogeneous head sensitivity, making non-uniform allocation futile.
9. **"If solver doesn't matter, why present MCKP at all?"** → (a) MCKP provides the formal framework for the constrained allocation problem — it's the lens through which we analyze the problem even if greedy solves it equally well, (b) presenting both solvers with identical results IS the evidence that the constraint is what matters, (c) for future extensions (more bit-widths, per-layer budgets), MCKP may regain advantage — we keep it as general framework.

1	Non-uniform per-head KV cache quantization helps only when head sensitivity exhibits a specific distribution shape---a finding obscured by prior work's focus on aggregate metrics.
2	We study seven models spanning 1.4B--14B parameters and five architecture families (MHA through GQA 8:1) on hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ and find that the benefit of per-head allocation depends not on GQA ratio or overall sensitivity magnitude, but on whether heterogeneity is \emph{spread} across multiple heads with cross-bitwidth gradients or concentrated in a single outlier.

6	We propose a joint empirical decision rule combining concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio) that correctly classifies all seven models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\ 14B spike).

Non-uniform per-head KV cache quantization helps only when head sensitivity exhibits a specific distribution shape---a finding obscured by prior work's focus on aggregate metrics.
We study seven models spanning 1.4B--14B parameters and five architecture families (MHA through GQA 8:1) on hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ and find that the benefit of per-head allocation depends not on GQA ratio or overall sensitivity magnitude, but on whether heterogeneity is \emph{spread} across multiple heads with cross-bitwidth gradients or concentrated in a single outlier.
On the one spread-pattern model (Qwen2.5-7B), a cardinality-constrained solver achieves 11.23 perplexity at $4\times$ compression---a 27.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45)---while unconstrained solvers fail catastrophically (32--37 PPL) due to 2-bit distortion compounding through the residual stream.
On the remaining six models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where scaling dilutes spread into spike---non-uniform allocation provides no meaningful benefit: Yi-1.5-9B has the highest concentration tested (0.71, exceeding Qwen-7B's 0.61) yet gains nothing, because its heterogeneity is a single-outlier ``spike'' with no cross-bitwidth gradient.
The cardinality constraint prevents catastrophic failure on spread architectures, moderate over-allocation on flat architectures (Gemma-2: unconstrained $1.47\times$ degradation reduced to within 0.5\% of uniform), and renders solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations---enabling a simple $O(H\log H)$ greedy algorithm.
We propose a joint empirical decision rule combining concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio) that correctly classifies all seven models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\ 14B spike).

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Per-head mixed-precision quantization of the KV cache is a natural strategy for reducing memory during LLM inference: assign fewer bits to insensitive heads and more bits to sensitive ones, achieving lower perplexity than uniform quantization at the same average bit-width.
5	Recent work on KV cache quantization explores both uniform schemes~\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant,lin2024qserve,he2024zipcache} and token-level mixed-precision approaches~\cite{ge2024fastgen,lei2026arkv}, while complementary methods reduce cache size through eviction~\cite{zhang2023h2o,li2024snapkv}.
6	RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalizes per-head allocation as a rate-distortion optimization and shows that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).
7	
8	In practice, hardware-efficient inference requires bit-widths drawn from $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$---the formats natively supported by modern accelerators.
9	On this non-consecutive set, the polymatroid structure breaks down, and greedy is no longer provably optimal.
10	One might expect that exact MCKP solvers would fill this gap.
11	They do not.
12	On Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression, unconstrained greedy achieves 32.45 PPL and unconstrained MCKP achieves 36.92---both \emph{far worse} than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
13	The optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.
14	
15	The root cause is not solver suboptimality but a violation of the additive distortion assumption.
16	Both solvers assign 68--75 of 112 KV heads to 2-bit, where per-head quantization errors compound through the residual stream.
17	The additive model predicts $\sim$11 PPL; the actual PPL is $3$--$4\times$ higher, because 2-bit distortions are orders of magnitude larger than 4-bit and compound super-linearly when many heads are quantized simultaneously.
18	
19	This observation points to a minimal intervention: cap the number of 2-bit assignments.
20	We add a single cardinality constraint $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h{=}2] \leq k$ to the standard MCKP formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}).
21	On Qwen2.5-7B, setting $k{=}8$ (7\% of heads) yields 11.23 PPL---a 27.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit.
22	The constraint works by forcing the solver to use 2-bit only on the least-sensitive heads, while redistributing the freed budget to protect sensitive heads at 8-bit or 16-bit.
23	This is not a heuristic patch: the constraint directly addresses the identified failure mode and is compatible with any solver.
24	The constraint is beneficial even on flat-distribution architectures: on Gemma-2-9B, unconstrained MCKP assigns 31.5\% of heads to 2-bit, producing a moderate $1.47\times$ degradation; the constraint reduces this to within 0.5\% of uniform.
25	
26	A surprising consequence is that the cardinality constraint renders solver choice irrelevant.
27	Constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations across all tested architectures (112/112 heads on Qwen, 256/256 on Llama, 255/256 on Mistral), enabling practitioners to use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm.
28	A per-layer brute-force oracle confirms near-optimality: the maximum gap is 0.02 PPL, 0.4\% of the total improvement (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).
29	
30	However, non-uniform allocation does not help universally.
31	On the remaining six models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where the $3.4\times$ increase in head count dilutes spread into spike---constrained MCKP provides no meaningful improvement.
32	The difference traces to the \emph{distribution shape} of head sensitivity, not GQA ratio or model scale alone: Qwen-7B's Layer-0 heads form a cluster of high sensitivity across multiple bitwidths (``spread''); Yi-1.5 and Qwen-14B have single extreme outliers (``spike''); Gemma-2, Mistral, and Pythia show near-uniform or mid-layer-concentrated sensitivity.
33	
34	This motivates a question prior work does not address: \emph{when} should a practitioner use per-head mixed-precision quantization?
35	We propose a joint empirical decision rule based on concentration and distribution shape (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) that correctly classifies all seven models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast.
36	Yi-1.5 is a critical test: its concentration ($0.71$) exceeds Qwen-7B's, but its single-outlier spike has no cross-bitwidth gradient, so MCKP cannot redistribute budget.
37	
38	Our contributions are:
39	\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
40	\item We identify 2-bit distortion compounding as the cause of catastrophic failure in unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths, and show that a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments is a minimal sufficient fix, reducing Qwen2.5-7B PPL from 32--37 (unconstrained) to 11.23 (constrained) at $4\times$ compression (\S\ref{sec:compounding}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}).
41	
42	\item We demonstrate that the cardinality constraint serves three roles: preventing catastrophic failure on spread architectures (Qwen: 32.45$\to$11.23), preventing moderate over-allocation on flat architectures (Gemma-2: 8.85$\to$within 0.5\% of uniform), and rendering solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce equivalent allocations across all tested architectures (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).
43	
44	\item We propose a joint empirical decision rule combining concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio) that correctly classifies all seven models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\ 14B spike) and a MHA architecture (Pythia-1.4B). Yi-1.5-9B serves as a critical test: its concentration exceeds Qwen-7B's, yet its single-outlier spike pattern means MCKP provides no benefit over uniform (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).
45	\end{enumerate}
46

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Per-head mixed-precision quantization of the KV cache is a natural strategy for reducing memory during LLM inference: assign fewer bits to insensitive heads and more bits to sensitive ones, achieving lower perplexity than uniform quantization at the same average bit-width.
Recent work on KV cache quantization explores both uniform schemes~\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant,lin2024qserve,he2024zipcache} and token-level mixed-precision approaches~\cite{ge2024fastgen,lei2026arkv}, while complementary methods reduce cache size through eviction~\cite{zhang2023h2o,li2024snapkv}.
RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalizes per-head allocation as a rate-distortion optimization and shows that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).

In practice, hardware-efficient inference requires bit-widths drawn from $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$---the formats natively supported by modern accelerators.
On this non-consecutive set, the polymatroid structure breaks down, and greedy is no longer provably optimal.
One might expect that exact MCKP solvers would fill this gap.
They do not.
On Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression, unconstrained greedy achieves 32.45 PPL and unconstrained MCKP achieves 36.92---both \emph{far worse} than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
The optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.

The root cause is not solver suboptimality but a violation of the additive distortion assumption.
Both solvers assign 68--75 of 112 KV heads to 2-bit, where per-head quantization errors compound through the residual stream.
The additive model predicts $\sim$11 PPL; the actual PPL is $3$--$4\times$ higher, because 2-bit distortions are orders of magnitude larger than 4-bit and compound super-linearly when many heads are quantized simultaneously.

This observation points to a minimal intervention: cap the number of 2-bit assignments.
We add a single cardinality constraint $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h{=}2] \leq k$ to the standard MCKP formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}).
On Qwen2.5-7B, setting $k{=}8$ (7\% of heads) yields 11.23 PPL---a 27.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit.
The constraint works by forcing the solver to use 2-bit only on the least-sensitive heads, while redistributing the freed budget to protect sensitive heads at 8-bit or 16-bit.
This is not a heuristic patch: the constraint directly addresses the identified failure mode and is compatible with any solver.
The constraint is beneficial even on flat-distribution architectures: on Gemma-2-9B, unconstrained MCKP assigns 31.5\% of heads to 2-bit, producing a moderate $1.47\times$ degradation; the constraint reduces this to within 0.5\% of uniform.

A surprising consequence is that the cardinality constraint renders solver choice irrelevant.
Constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations across all tested architectures (112/112 heads on Qwen, 256/256 on Llama, 255/256 on Mistral), enabling practitioners to use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm.
A per-layer brute-force oracle confirms near-optimality: the maximum gap is 0.02 PPL, 0.4\% of the total improvement (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).

However, non-uniform allocation does not help universally.
On the remaining six models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where the $3.4\times$ increase in head count dilutes spread into spike---constrained MCKP provides no meaningful improvement.
The difference traces to the \emph{distribution shape} of head sensitivity, not GQA ratio or model scale alone: Qwen-7B's Layer-0 heads form a cluster of high sensitivity across multiple bitwidths (``spread''); Yi-1.5 and Qwen-14B have single extreme outliers (``spike''); Gemma-2, Mistral, and Pythia show near-uniform or mid-layer-concentrated sensitivity.

This motivates a question prior work does not address: \emph{when} should a practitioner use per-head mixed-precision quantization?
We propose a joint empirical decision rule based on concentration and distribution shape (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) that correctly classifies all seven models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast.
Yi-1.5 is a critical test: its concentration ($0.71$) exceeds Qwen-7B's, but its single-outlier spike has no cross-bitwidth gradient, so MCKP cannot redistribute budget.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item We identify 2-bit distortion compounding as the cause of catastrophic failure in unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths, and show that a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments is a minimal sufficient fix, reducing Qwen2.5-7B PPL from 32--37 (unconstrained) to 11.23 (constrained) at $4\times$ compression (\S\ref{sec:compounding}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}).

\item We demonstrate that the cardinality constraint serves three roles: preventing catastrophic failure on spread architectures (Qwen: 32.45$\to$11.23), preventing moderate over-allocation on flat architectures (Gemma-2: 8.85$\to$within 0.5\% of uniform), and rendering solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce equivalent allocations across all tested architectures (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).

\item We propose a joint empirical decision rule combining concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio) that correctly classifies all seven models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\ 14B spike) and a MHA architecture (Pythia-1.4B). Yi-1.5-9B serves as a critical test: its concentration exceeds Qwen-7B's, yet its single-outlier spike pattern means MCKP provides no benefit over uniform (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
5	\label{sec:formulation}
6	
7	We formulate per-head KV cache quantization as a constrained optimization problem.
8	Let $h \in \{1,\ldots,H\}$ index the KV heads across all layers, $b_h \in \mathcal{B}$ the bit-width assigned to head $h$, and $\mathcal{B} = \{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ the set of hardware-aligned bit-widths.
9	Each head $h$ has a profiled distortion function $d_h(b)$, the PPL increase when head $h$ is quantized to $b$ bits.
10	Given a memory budget ratio $R$ (e.g., $R = 0.25$ for $4\times$ compression), we seek the allocation that minimizes total distortion:
11	\begin{equation}
12	\label{eq:objective}
13	\min_{\{b_h\}} \sum_{h=1}^{H} d_h(b_h) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \frac{1}{H \cdot 16}\sum_{h=1}^{H} b_h \leq R.
14	\end{equation}
15	
16	This is a multiple-choice knapsack problem (MCKP): each head selects one bit-width from $\mathcal{B}$ to minimize total distortion under a budget.
17	RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} solves this for consecutive bit-widths $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, where the polymatroid structure of the feasible set guarantees that greedy allocation is optimal (their Proposition 6).
18	Hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ are non-consecutive; the gaps break this structure, and greedy is no longer guaranteed to match the MCKP optimum.
19	Moreover, as we show in \S\ref{sec:compounding}, the objective itself is not well-behaved: distortions from 2-bit heads compound non-additively, making unconstrained optimization unreliable.
20	
21	\subsection{PPL-based Per-Head Profiling}
22	\label{sec:profiling}
23	
24	We use symmetric per-channel quantization with per-head granularity: each KV head is independently quantized to one of the candidate bit-widths $\mathcal{B} = \{2, 4, 8, 16\}$, without per-token scaling.
25	We profile each head by quantizing it to each $b \in \mathcal{B}$ while keeping all other heads at bf16, and measuring the resulting PPL increase $d_h(b)$ on a calibration set of 64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train.
26	This yields a distortion table of $H \times |\mathcal{B}|$ entries that serves as input to the solver.
27	
28	The optimization in Eq.~\eqref{eq:objective} relies on an additive distortion assumption: the total PPL degradation from a mixed-precision allocation is approximately $\sum_h d_h(b_h)$.
29	This holds when per-head distortions are small and independent---a reasonable approximation for 4-bit and 8-bit quantization, where individual head distortions are typically below 0.1 PPL.
30	At 2-bit, however, individual distortions are orders of magnitude larger, and the additive assumption breaks down.
31	
32	\subsection{Compounding Effect}
33	\label{sec:compounding}
34	
35	When many heads are simultaneously quantized to 2-bit, per-head distortions compound non-additively: truncation errors from multiple 2-bit heads accumulate through the residual stream, and once their count exceeds the network's capacity to compensate, PPL degrades super-linearly.
36	
37	Unconstrained solvers are blind to this effect because the additive objective underestimates the cost of large-scale 2-bit assignment.
38	On Qwen2.5-7B, unconstrained greedy assigns 68 heads to 2-bit and achieves 32.45 PPL; unconstrained MCKP assigns 75 heads and achieves 36.92---both far worse than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
39	Standard-resolution profiling detects non-zero $d_h(2)$ for only 37 of 112 heads; the remaining 75 heads have $d_h(2) \approx 0$, so most 2-bit assignments appear free to the additive objective.
40	The resulting additive prediction is $\sum_h d_h(b_h) + \text{baseline} \approx 11$ PPL---$3\text{--}4\times$ lower than the actual 32--37 PPL, because the compounding interaction between simultaneously quantized heads is invisible to per-head profiling.
41	
42	This compounding is specific to 2-bit quantization and is \emph{super-additive}: quantizing the top-$k$ most sensitive heads to 2-bit simultaneously produces PPL $1.56\times$ the sum of their individual distortions at $k{=}8$, growing to $4.89\times$ at $k{=}64$.
43	A random-$k$ control confirms that sensitivity ordering matters: at $k{=}64$, random selection yields 55.94 PPL vs.\ 22.95 for top-$k$, because random draws are more likely to include high-distortion heads that amplify compounding.
44	At 4-bit and above, per-head distortions are small enough that additivity holds even when all heads share the same bit-width (uniform 4-bit achieves 15.45 PPL, close to the sum-of-distortions prediction).
45	The qualitative difference arises because 2-bit quantization has far larger per-head distortion, saturating the error tolerance of the residual stream.
46	
47	The relationship between $k$ and PPL is U-shaped (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}, Appendix~\ref{sec:compounding_appendix}): at $k{=}0$ (uniform 4-bit), PPL is 15.45; allowing a few 2-bit heads reduces PPL by freeing budget for 8-bit heads on sensitive positions, reaching a minimum of 11.23 at $k{=}8$; beyond $k{=}8$, compounding drives PPL upward.
48	
49	\subsection{Cardinality Constraint}
50	\label{sec:cardinality}
51	
52	The compounding effect motivates a simple addition to Eq.~\eqref{eq:objective}: a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments.
53	\begin{equation}
54	\label{eq:constraint}
55	\sum_{h=1}^{H} \mathbb{1}[b_h = 2] \leq k.
56	\end{equation}
57	
58	The constraint parameter $k$ is selected by a small-scale sweep on calibration data: solve the constrained problem for each candidate $k$, evaluate calibration PPL, and pick the value at the minimum of the U-shaped curve (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}).
59	For Qwen2.5-7B with 112 KV heads, $k{=}8$ ($\sim$7\% of heads).
60	
61	The constraint is a single linear inequality, compatible with any solver---greedy, MCKP, or integer linear programming---and adds negligible overhead to the optimization.
62	
63	One might expect Layer-0 heads to require explicit protection.
64	On Qwen2.5-7B, however, the profiler assigns very high 2-bit distortion to Layer-0 heads (L0H0: $+$31.9\%, L0H2: $+$23.2\%, L0H3: $+$11.7\% relative to bf16), so no solver would assign them 2-bit under any reasonable budget.
65	Running the solver with and without manual Layer-0 exclusion produces identical allocations; no manual rule is needed.
66	
67	\paragraph{Restoring additivity.}
68	The additive objective treats per-head distortions as independent, but 2-bit compounding violates this once many 2-bit heads coexist.
69	Restricting 2-bit heads to $k \ll H$ pushes the allocation back into a near-additive regime where the profiler's prediction agrees with measured PPL.
70	For Qwen2.5-7B, $k{=}8$ ($\sim$7\% of heads) is few enough that compounding contributes negligibly, consistent with the U-shaped curve minimum (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}).
71	This explains the constrained--unconstrained gap in Table~\ref{tab:solver_equiv}: constrained greedy operates inside the additive regime (11.23 PPL, matching the ${\approx}11$ additive estimate), while unconstrained solvers extrapolate outside it and miss true PPL by $3\text{--}4\times$.
72	
73	\subsection{Solver Equivalence}
74	\label{sec:solver_equiv}
75	
76	\begin{table}[t]
77	\centering
78	\small
79	\caption{Solver comparison on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression. Unconstrained solvers over-allocate 2-bit heads and fail catastrophically. The cardinality constraint ($k{\leq}8$) makes greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations.\protect\footnotemark}
80	\label{tab:solver_equiv}
81	\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
82	\toprule
83	Solver & Constraint & PPL & \multicolumn{3}{c}{Bit distribution} \\
84	 & & & 2-bit & 4-bit & 8/16-bit \\
85	\midrule
86	Greedy & None & 32.45 & 68 & 30 & 14 \\
87	MCKP & None & 36.92 & 75 & 33 & 4 \\
88	Greedy & $k{\leq}8$ & 11.23 & 8 & 100 & 4 \\
89	MCKP & $k{\leq}8$ & 11.23 & 8 & 100 & 4 \\
90	Uniform & --- & 15.45 & 0 & 112 & 0 \\
91	\bottomrule
92	\end{tabular}
93	\end{table}
94	\footnotetext{Standard-resolution profiling; hires profiling (64 seq $\times$ 2048 tok) achieves 10.91 (Appendix~\ref{sec:profiling_resolution}).}
95	
96	With the cardinality constraint, greedy and MCKP produce identical results (Table~\ref{tab:solver_equiv}): same PPL (11.23), same bit distribution on Qwen2.5-7B.
97	
98	\paragraph{Empirical observation.}
99	When $k \ll H$ and the top-$k$ heads ranked by marginal benefit $d_h(4) - d_h(2)$ contain no ties, constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical per-head allocations.
100	The constraint restricts the feasible set so that the only decision is which $k$ heads to assign 2-bit; the marginal-benefit ordering determines this uniquely, so greedy's local choice coincides with the global optimum.
101	We verify this across three architectures: Qwen2.5-7B (112/112 heads identical), Llama-3.1-8B (256/256), Mistral-7B-v0.3 (255/256; the single difference is a zero-distortion tie with no PPL impact).
102	Without the constraint, greedy cascades into excessive 2-bit allocation, as each additional 2-bit head looks locally beneficial but contributes to compounding.
103	Practitioners can therefore use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm without sacrificing optimality.
104	
105	A per-layer brute-force oracle on Qwen2.5-7B confirms near-optimality: of 8 layers with non-trivial allocations, MCKP matches the oracle on 5; the remaining 3 have a maximum gap of 0.018 PPL (0.4\% of the total improvement), closing the optimality chain from greedy through MCKP to brute-force.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Models.}
8	We evaluate seven models spanning five architecture families and diverse attention configurations:
9	\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA 7:1, 28 layers $\times$ 4 KV heads = 112),
10	\textbf{Qwen2.5-14B} (GQA 5:1, 48 $\times$ 8 = 384),
11	\textbf{Yi-1.5-9B} (GQA 8:1, 48 $\times$ 4 = 192),
12	\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256),
13	\textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256, sliding window attention),
14	\textbf{Gemma-2-9B} (GQA 2:1, 42 $\times$ 8 = 336, \texttt{head\_dim}=256, attention logit softcapping),
15	and \textbf{Pythia-1.4B} (MHA 1:1, 24 $\times$ 16 = 384).
16	This selection spans GQA ratios from 1:1 (MHA) to 8:1 and covers standard, sliding-window, softcapped, and multi-head attention.
17	
18	\paragraph{Evaluation.}
19	We report perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.
20	For downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.
21

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Models.}
We evaluate seven models spanning five architecture families and diverse attention configurations:
\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA 7:1, 28 layers $\times$ 4 KV heads = 112),
\textbf{Qwen2.5-14B} (GQA 5:1, 48 $\times$ 8 = 384),
\textbf{Yi-1.5-9B} (GQA 8:1, 48 $\times$ 4 = 192),
\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256),
\textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256, sliding window attention),
\textbf{Gemma-2-9B} (GQA 2:1, 42 $\times$ 8 = 336, \texttt{head\_dim}=256, attention logit softcapping),
and \textbf{Pythia-1.4B} (MHA 1:1, 24 $\times$ 16 = 384).
This selection spans GQA ratios from 1:1 (MHA) to 8:1 and covers standard, sliding-window, softcapped, and multi-head attention.

\paragraph{Evaluation.}
We report perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.
For downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.

\paragraph{Profiling.}
Per-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.
We use two profiling resolutions: \emph{standard} (16 sequences $\times$ 512 tokens) and \emph{high-resolution} (64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens), both from WikiText-2 train.
Unless marked with $\dagger$, all results use standard-resolution profiling; Appendix~\ref{sec:profiling_resolution} analyzes the effect of resolution.

\paragraph{Compression and constraint.}
The default target is 4$\times$ compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio 0.25).
The cardinality constraint limits 2-bit assignments to at most $k$ heads, where $k$ is selected via the compounding sweep described in \S\ref{sec:method} ($k{=}8$ for Qwen-7B, $k{=}2$ for Yi-1.5 and Llama, $k{=}4$ for Mistral, $k{=}8$ for Gemma-2; Qwen-14B and Pythia $k$ values pending).

\paragraph{Baselines.}
We compare against:
(1)~uniform 4-bit quantization;
(2)~unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style~\cite{zuo2026ratequant});
(3)~unconstrained MCKP allocation;
(4)~an L0-random heuristic that assigns Layer-0 heads to 8-bit and $k$ random non-Layer-0 heads to 2-bit, with remaining heads at 4-bit (5 seeds; we report mean$\pm$std and median);
and (5)~a naive positional heuristic that assigns Layer-0 to 8-bit and the $k$ deepest heads to 2-bit.

\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main_results}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{PPL ($\downarrow$) on WikiText-2 at 4$\times$ compression. Unconstrained failure severity tracks heterogeneity shape: catastrophic on Qwen-7B ($3.3\times$ bf16), moderate on Gemma-2 ($1.5\times$), mild on the remaining models (${\sim}1.1\times$). Best constrained result per model in \textbf{bold}; --- = experiment pending. $^\dagger$Hires profiling (64 seq $\times$ 2048 tok). $^\ddagger$Best $k$ from ablation ($k{=}4$). $^*$BOS-corrected.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
Model & Baseline & Uniform & Uncons. & Ours \\
 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & MCKP & (Constr.) \\
\midrule
Qwen2.5-7B      & 9.81  & 15.45 & 36.92 & \textbf{11.23} \\
Qwen2.5-14B     & 5.84  & ---   & ---   & --- \\
Yi-1.5-9B$^\dagger$       & 7.02  & 7.22  & 7.56  & 7.22 \\
Llama-3.1-8B$^\dagger$    & 8.09  & 8.47  & 8.63  & \textbf{8.45} \\
Mistral-7B-v0.3$^\dagger$ & 7.04  & 7.13  & 7.57  & 7.16$^\ddagger$ \\
Gemma-2-9B$^{*\dagger}$   & 6.03  & 6.17  & 8.85  & 6.20 \\
Pythia-1.4B     & 13.63 & ---   & ---   & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

On Qwen2.5-7B, constrained MCKP achieves 11.23 PPL, a 27.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45); hires profiling further improves this to 10.91 (Appendix~\ref{sec:profiling_resolution}).
Without the constraint, both greedy (32.45) and MCKP (36.92) perform \emph{worse} than uniform---a catastrophic failure from excessive 2-bit assignments compounding across layers.
Across 3 calibration seeds, constrained MCKP yields mean PPL 10.99$\pm$0.06 with 90.2\% three-way allocation agreement, confirming profiling stability.

On Llama-3.1-8B, the result is essentially indistinguishable from uniform (8.45 vs.\ 8.47, $\Delta < 0.02$ PPL).
Hires profiling reveals a spike pattern (concentration 0.57, $t_1/t_5{=}0.85$) dominated by a single top head (L2H5), leaving little cross-bitwidth gradient for non-uniform allocation to exploit.

On Mistral-7B-v0.3, constrained MCKP (7.16, $k{=}4$) is slightly worse than uniform (7.13, $+$0.4\%)---a genuine negative result, as the profiler reports near-zero sensitivity differences across heads.
Mistral's sliding-window attention may contribute to this uniformity.

On Yi-1.5-9B$^\dagger$, constrained MCKP ($k{=}2$) matches uniform at 7.22 PPL.
Despite the highest concentration tested (0.71), sensitivity is dominated by a single outlier (L4H3, $t_1/t_5{=}0.90$), a spike pattern with no cross-bitwidth gradient to exploit.

On Gemma-2-9B$^*$ (GQA 2:1), constrained MCKP ($k{=}8$) achieves 6.20 PPL vs.\ uniform 6.17, slightly above ($+$0.4\%).
Despite its flat sensitivity distribution (concentration 0.23), unconstrained MCKP degrades to 8.85 ($1.47\times$ bf16)---a moderate failure driven by the solver assigning 31.5\% of heads to 2-bit (vs.\ 4.7--16.4\% in other non-spread models).
The constraint reduces 2-bit heads from 106 to 8, confirming that it universally prevents over-allocation regardless of distribution shape.

Unconstrained failure severity tracks heterogeneity shape: catastrophic on Qwen ($3.3\times$ bf16), moderate on Gemma-2 ($1.47\times$), mild on the remaining three (${\sim}1.07$--$1.08\times$).
The allocation visualization (Figure~\ref{fig:allocation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:allocation_appendix}) and budget sweep (Appendix~\ref{sec:budget_sweep}) provide additional detail.

MCKP consistently outperforms random L0-constrained allocation and naive positional baselines across all three tested models (median gap 5--16\%; Table~\ref{tab:heuristic} in Appendix~\ref{sec:heuristic_appendix}).

\subsection{Downstream Evaluation}
\label{sec:downstream}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{0-shot accuracy change (Ours $-$ Uniform, pts) at 4$\times$ compression. Qwen shows large gains; the remaining models show small degradations or neutrality, tracking PPL results. $^\dagger$Hires profiling.}
\label{tab:downstream}
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
Model & ARC-C & HS & PIQA & WG & Avg \\
\midrule
Qwen2.5-7B        & $+$3.2 & $+$4.0 & $+$1.3 & $+$2.0 & $+$2.6 \\
Yi-1.5-9B$^\dagger$        & $-$3.2 & $-$0.6 & $-$0.3 & $+$1.3 & $-$0.8 \\
Llama-3.1-8B$^\dagger$     & $-$2.7 & $-$0.1 & $-$0.7 & $-$0.2 & $-$1.0 \\
Mistral-7B$^\dagger$       & $-$1.2 & $-$0.2 & $+$0.4 & $-$1.0 & $-$0.5 \\
Gemma-2-9B$^\dagger$       & $-$0.2 & $+$0.3 & $-$0.1 & $+$0.8 & $+$0.1 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

On Qwen, constrained MCKP improves average 0-shot accuracy by 2.6 pts over uniform (0.686 vs.\ 0.660), recovering $\sim$73\% of the accuracy lost to quantization.
The four non-spread architectures show minor average degradation (Yi $-$0.8, Llama $-$1.0, Mistral $-$0.5, Gemma-2 $+$0.1 pts).
ARC-Challenge shows the largest per-task sensitivity across all models (Yi $-$3.2, Llama $-$2.7, Mistral $-$1.2, Gemma-2 $-$0.2 pts), consistent with multi-step reasoning where KV cache errors accumulate.
Cross-dataset stability analysis (Appendix~\ref{sec:cross_dataset}) confirms ${>}96\%$ bit-assignment agreement between WikiText-2 and C4 calibration across all three tested models.

[飞书用户 曹晓玉 (ou_ed2f4ceeab862a8049a88352dc56181e)]: 他说的这个是什么意思？对吗？：Method 改进分析——理论与实验两端
核心判断
方法的瓶颈是 architectural 的，不是 algorithmic 的：
1. Per-channel asymmetric quantization (KIVI) 完全 subsumes per-head allocation 信号（KIVI 9.90 vs 我们 10.91，差距 100% 来自量化方案）
2. Spread pattern 是稀有现象（1/9 模型），这是 architecture/training 性质，solver 改不了
理论层面——3 个可改进方向
方向                            | 理论吸引力 | 实际收益上界                  | 9天可行性                         
--------------------------------+------------+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------
Per-layer k（每层独立约束）     | 高         | ≤0.02 PPL（oracle gap）      | 可做但收益极低                    
Non-additive pairwise profiling | 高         | 低（L0 heuristic 已捕获 93%） | 不可行（O(H²) forward passes）   
Weighted/adaptive k             | 中         | 未知                          | 违背 static offline 设计，scope 外

结论：constraint 本身已接近最优（brute-force oracle 只比 MCKP 好 0.02 PPL）。算法层面能挤出的空间 <0.1 PPL。
实验层面——真正能提分的方向
唯一能改变 paper story 的实验：KIVI + constraint 组合
核心问题：在 KIVI asymmetric quantization 下，unconstrained allocation 是否仍会 compound？
- 如果 compound 仍存在 → constraint 有独立价值，不被 KIVI subsume → 论文通用性大增，从"symmetric-only niche"升级为"universal safeguard"
- 如果 compound 消失 → 确认 per-channel asymmetric 能天然抑制 compounding → 论文 scope 不变但更诚实
脚本已写好（Reviewer PASS），等 multi-seed 完成后立即跑（~2-3h GPU time）。
具体建议方案
立即可做（已在执行）：
1. ✅ KIVI asymmetric compounding test — 最高优先级，直接回应 Dream reviewer #1 攻击点
2. ✅ Solver equivalence verify (Llama/Mistral) — 关闭 claim 验证缺口，30min
值得但 9 天来不及做深的：
3. Long-context aware profiling — 用 8K data 做 profiling 替代 2K，看 Qwen long-context 收益是否进一步提升
4. KIVI + constraint 正向组合 — 不是测 compounding，而是测"KIVI asymmetric + per-head constraint = 是否比 KIVI alone 更好"
不值得做的：
- Per-layer k optimization（上界 0.02 PPL，diminishing returns）
- Additional model families（N=1 已诚实声明，加 1-2 个不改变结论）
- Interaction-aware profiling（实现复杂，L0 heuristic 93% 说明交互效应被现有方法覆盖）
底线
如果 KIVI compounding 实验成功（compounding 在 asymmetric 下仍存在），论文从 "niche contribution for symmetric-only" 升级为 "universal safeguard regardless of quantization scheme"。这是 9 天内唯一能实质性改变分数的实验。其他方向要么收益上界太低（<0.1 PPL），要么来不及做深。
